built_up_area.source: Cornell, Beginnings of Rome 1995 (modern synthesis); Platner-Ashby s.v. Roma
built_up_area.text: Settlement concentrated on the Palatine, Capitol, Velia and the Forum valley, with extensions on the lower Esquiline, Caelian and Quirinal; fortified in parts by a 6th-century wall and an agger on the east.
After the Gallic sack (390), rebuilding on the old street plan was said to be hasty (Livy 5.55.2-5).

built_up_area.source: Livy 6.32.1; Platner-Ashby s.v. Murus Servii Tullii
built_up_area.text: City enclosed by the Servian Wall: circuit about 11 km, area about 426 ha; seven hills and the Forum within, the Campus Martius and Aventine suburbs outside (Aventine within the pomerium only from Claudius).
Growth outside the wall: Campus Martius (Circus Flaminius, porticoes), Emporium and Aventine riverside, Trastevere. Concrete tenements (insulae) and the first horrea.

built_up_area.source: Modern estimates, Platner-Ashby s.v. Roma; the Aurelian Wall area is documented in Lanciani Forma Urbis
built_up_area.text: Built-up area spills well beyond the Servian Wall: Campus Martius (Theatre of Pompey, Saepta), Trastevere, Esquiline and Via Appia. Roughly 1,300-1,800 ha continuously built by the end of the period (modern estimate); the Aurelian Wall (AD 271) later encloses 1,373 ha.

census_figures.source: Dion. Hal. 5.20.3 gives 130,000 for the first census of the Republic; the figure is probably invented)
Phlegon of Tralles (FGrH 257 F 12); Livy Per. 98 has 900,000; reflects enfranchisement of Italians after the Social War
Res Gestae 8 (4,063,000 in 28 BC; 4,233,000 in 8 BC); includes women and children probably not counted in earlier censuses

grain_dole.what: C. Gracchus' grain law: monthly grain at a fixed price to citizens (Plut. C. Gracchus 5; Livy Per. 60)
Clodius' law makes the grain free (Cic. Sest. 55; Asc. Pis. 8)
Cato extends the dole (Plut. Cato Minor 26)
number of recipients before Caesar's census, reduced to 150,000 afterward (Suet. Iul. 41.3)
after Caesar's revision of the lists (Suet. Iul. 41.3; Plut. Caes. 55)
Augustus' distribution to the plebs urbana in 2 BC (Res Gestae 15.4); outside the 27 BC limit

note_census: Before 70 BC, the figures are adult male citizens (assidui) of the whole Roman state, almost all of them farmers outside the city; they cannot be turned into a population for the city itself. The 4 million of 28 BC counts all citizens (the counting rule changed).
